page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, providing 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance includes 16 GB of system RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates cryptographic instructions such as AES and SHA-NI, alongside AVX, BMI2, ADX, and FMA extensions.

Benchmark assessments indicate modest compute performance across synthetic tests. Single-core results show a Geekbench score of 1282.0 and a bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 9.2 GB/sec, placing it in the average tier. However, multi-core throughput is constrained, registering a PassMark CPU score of 5552.37, a Geekbench multi-core score of 2859.0, and stress-ng multi-core performance of 1531.17, placing these within the lower percentiles. Memory testing demonstrates average overall throughput with a PassMark memory score of 2155.72 and 31.83 GB/sec large-block uncached read speeds.

Architectural tradeoffs center on external dependency for persistence and data transport. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers 3.6 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.96 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Cost efficiency is defined by its balanced resource configuration without dedicated accelerator overhead, making it suitable for standard web serving, small databases, staging environments, and intermediate enterprise microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of memory, built on an AMD EPYC 7H12 x86_64 processor operating at 2.6 GHz across 2 physical cores. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reveal mid-tier single-threaded capability alongside constrained multi-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1282.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 5552.37. Memory operations achieve a balanced profile with 31.83 GB/sec large-block uncached read speeds. The standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a practical resource balance for general workloads that do not demand extreme CPU parallelization or heavy I/O throughput, such as lightweight web servers, background task runners, small internal databases, and test or development environments.
